request: Analyze GSE228901 for PMID 37059838 (Protectin DX as a therapeutic strategy against frailty in mice.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk polyA RNA-seq, female mouse liver (S2.8.p1, S2.9.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: 15 female livers, 5 per group: Adult (6 mo, vehicle), Old (22 mo, vehicle), PDX (22 mo, Protectin DX gavage 9 wk) (S3.7.p1)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of aging (Old vs Adult) and of Protectin DX treatment (PDX vs Old) on liver gene expression. The study has no exercise intervention: treadmill exhaustion and voluntary wheel running are physical-performance assessments given to every mouse in every group (S2.2.p1, S2.4.p1, S2.4.p7, S2.4.p9).
planned_contrasts: Old vs Adult (aging; S3.7.p2: 1,621 genes at FDR q < 0.05)
PDX vs Old (drug; S3.7.p2: 0 genes at FDR q < 0.25)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 Wald test, pairwise groups, BH FDR; featureCounts Ensembl gene counts (S2.9.p1-p2)
final.paper_results: Old vs Adult 1,621 DEGs FDR<0.05; PDX vs Old 0 DEGs FDR<0.25; Hallmark GSEA (S3.7.p3)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: The paper is a pharmacological (PDX) and aging study. Exercise appears only as endpoint fitness tests (treadmill to exhaustion, 4-day voluntary wheel in activity cages) applied to all groups at baseline and endpoint (S2.4.p1-p9); no group was trained or kept sedentary. The words exercise/training do not occur in the article.

ownership.reasoning: Paper S2.9.p3 deposits GSE228901; GEO metadata (liver, female cohort, vehicle/PDX, 6 vs 22 months) matches S3.7.p1.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns A1..P5 equal the metadata title column (inspect alignment_keys: 15/15). Group letter from title agrees with the age and treatment characteristics.

matrix.reasoning: integer_fraction 1.0, max 4.2e6; data_processing and S2.9.p1 state featureCounts gene-level counts. The VST file is a derived log-scale matrix and is not used.

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast: the three arms (Adult vehicle, Old vehicle, Old PDX) differ by age and drug only. Treadmill distance and voluntary wheel km/d in the metadata are per-animal fitness test readouts, not an assigned exercise exposure; regressing expression on them would be an associational fitness analysis the paper never planned. The paper's own contrasts (aging, PDX) do not answer how exercise affects gene expression.

candidates.value: regression on treadmill distance or voluntary wheel km/d
candidates.reason_rejected: fitness test outcome measured in all animals, confounded with age (Adult 67-101 m vs Old 34-79 m); not an exercise intervention and not planned by the paper

design.reasoning: Paper S2.2.p1/S2.4 define treadmill and wheel as physical performance assessments in every group; there is no exercised vs sedentary arm. Refused at design.

discrepancies.item: Requested estimand (exercise effect) vs study design
discrepancies.paper: Aging and Protectin DX study; exercise only as fitness testing in all groups (S2.4)
discrepancies.data: GEO groups: age (6 vs 22 months) and treatment (vehicle vs PDX); treadmill/wheel are continuous per-animal readouts
